# CHS-A golden vectors -- captured off the real M20S, 2026-09-15
#
# Source: a live plaintext TCP session to 10.21.33.103:30003 (chassis serial
# CM20200041, robot_server 3.1.1), recorded by data/run/chassis/dump_raw.py.
# These are the bytes the chassis ACCEPTED from us and the bytes it SENT back.
#
# Why they are captured rather than generated. A golden vector produced by the
# encoder under test cannot disagree with it -- it would prove only that the
# code equals itself. These came off the wire, so they pin the three things the
# field tables do not say out loud: the PatrolDevice wrapper, the mandatory
# Time field, and the 32-bit codes serialised as DECIMAL (0x00100064 ->
# 1048676). A "cleanup" to hex strings breaks the decode of every line here.
#
# Format: <tag> <byte count> <lowercase hex of the WHOLE frame, header included>
# TX_* is a frame we sent; RX_* is a frame the chassis sent, tagged with its
# Type and Command in hex so the routing assertions read against the code book.
#
# Re-capture (chassis powered, plaintext mode):
#   ssh xbrain 'cd /opt/xbrain_v6/data/run/chassis && \
#     python3 dump_raw.py 10.21.33.103 30003 8'
